blocking.title: D4 matcher misses scripts and data that CI gates run on (scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json, scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json), so a PR changing them comes back mergedBy 'auto-merge'
blocking.failurePath:
ADR 0021 D4 (line 37) routes the scripts and data that CI and .husky call to a user merge. The rule text is "CI 与 .husky 调用的其余脚本和数据". Its parenthetical names only scripts/check-*, lint-warning-cap.mjs, pack-smoke.sh and ui-consumer-registry.json, and PROTECTED at pr-gate.js:29-47 copies exactly that list.

At the head, CI also runs code and reads data the list omits:
- scripts/ui-normalize.mjs is imported by ui-registry-gate.mjs (import at line 79), ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs:54 and ui-drift-gate.mjs:69. ci.yml runs all three at lines 101, 108 and 191.
- scripts/ui-registry.json is the manifest and hash ledger. ui-registry-gate.mjs:84 and ui-dead-class-gate.mjs:765 read it (ci.yml:311).
- scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json is read by ui-registry-gate.mjs:86.

Trace with args changedFiles ['scripts/ui-normalize.mjs'], deletedFiles [], linesChanged 10, and a safety list equal to changedFiles:
1. matchedProtected at line 96 is [], so the safety prompt at line 124 says 'none'.
2. protectedPaths is [] unless an LLM reviewer happens to add the path.
3. humanReasons at lines 273-278 is [].
4. The result is mergedBy 'auto-merge' and go true.

I reproduced this with stub agents. The same output comes back for scripts/ui-registry.json and scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json.

Under spec 28 D7, the session then enables auto-merge without the user. A PR could make hashFile in ui-normalize.mjs return the ledger value, or re-freeze ui-registry.json, and so weaken the components/ui registry gate. That is the 'agent edits its own gate' case D4 exists to prevent, and the script comment at lines 25-28 says routing should not depend on a reviewer remembering it.

The PR body says 4c27770 took run 2's suggestion on 'the CI scripts outside scripts/*gate*'. The fix covers only the four files the ADR lists.
blocking.evidence: git show 3b0da7b:scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs lines 26-31 list its inputs as scripts/ui-registry.json, scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json and scripts/ui-normalize.mjs. The probe output: 'scripts/ui-normalize.mjs -> go true mergedBy auto-merge', 'scripts/ui-registry.json -> go true mergedBy auto-merge', 'scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json -> go true mergedBy auto-merge'. ADR 0021 D4's parenthetical, which presents itself as the list of the remaining CI and husky scripts and data, is therefore also wrong at the head. Fix: add the three paths to PROTECTED and to ADR 0021 D4. A broader alternative is to protect every scripts/** file that a .github/workflows step or a gate script references.
skeptics:
I could not refute the finding. The failure is real at 3b0da7b.

How the matcher behaves:
- PROTECTED is at pr-gate.js:29-47. The glob converter (globToRegExp, :49-63) turns '*' into [^/]*.
- None of 'scripts/*gate*', 'scripts/*baseline*.json', 'scripts/check-*', the three named script and data files, or '**/package.json' matches scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json or scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json.
- As a result, matchedProtected (:96) is empty, and the safety prompt (:124) says 'none'.
- protectedPaths (:264-270) gets these paths only if a reviewer volunteers them.
- humanReasons (:273-278) stays empty, so mergedBy is 'auto-merge' (:297).

I checked this by running the head script with my own stub agents (written separately, not the PR's harness). For each of the three files as changedFiles, with linesChanged 10, the result was go true, mergedBy auto-merge, and protectedPaths []. The control cases scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs and scripts/lint-warning-cap.mjs route to the user, as expected.

CI does depend on these files at the head:
- ui-registry-gate.mjs:79 imports hashFile from ./ui-normalize.mjs.
- ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs:54 and ui-drift-gate.mjs:69 import stripCodeComments from it.
- ui-registry-gate.mjs:84-87 reads scripts/ui-registry.json and scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json.
- ui-dead-class-gate.mjs:765 reads ui-registry.json.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml runs these gates at lines 101, 108, 191 and 311.

The ADR also covers them:
- ADR 0021 D4 (line 37) routes 'CI 与 .husky 调用的其余脚本和数据' to the user.
- These files are scripts and data that CI uses. They are the same kind of file as scripts/ui-consumer-registry.json, which the list does protect.
- Spec 28 D7/§7.4 has the session enable auto-merge for PRs that do not hit D4.

So a PR that changes hashFile, or re-freezes the ledger, can weaken the components/ui registry gate and still be merged without the user. The finding stands.

The finding is real at 3b0da7b.

1. PROTECTED in .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js (lines 29-47) has no glob that matches scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json or scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json. None of the three names contains "gate", ".json" files without "baseline" miss scripts/*baseline*.json, and the list names only ui-consumer-registry.json explicitly.

2. CI does depend on all three files:
- scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs:79 imports hashFile and isHashShape from ./ui-normalize.mjs.
- ui-registry-gate.mjs:84 and :86 read scripts/ui-registry.json and scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json.
- ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs:54 and ui-drift-gate.mjs:69 also import ui-normalize.mjs.
- ui-dead-class-gate.mjs:765 reads ui-registry.json.
- ci.yml runs these gates at lines 101, 108, 191 and 311.

3. ADR 0021 D4's category text is "CI 与 .husky 调用的其余脚本和数据", and these files fall under it. The parenthetical list is incomplete: it names ui-consumer-registry.json, the data file of ui-consumer-shape-gate, but leaves out ui-registry.json, the equivalent ledger of ui-registry-gate.

4. I ran the head script with stub agents that returned no findings and no extra protectedPaths. Args were changedFiles=[f], deletedFiles=[], linesChanged=10, and the safety reviewer's changedFiles was [f].
- scripts/ui-normalize.mjs returned go true, mergedBy auto-merge, protectedPaths [].
- scripts/ui-registry.json returned go true, mergedBy auto-merge, protectedPaths [].
- scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json returned go true, mergedBy auto-merge, protectedPaths [].
- The control, scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs, returned mergedBy user.
- The safety prompt said "none" for the first three, so the routing depends only on an LLM reviewer adding the path.
- Under spec 28 D7 and §7.5, go with mergedBy auto-merge leads the session to turn on auto-merge without the user. A PR that edits hashFile, or that re-freezes the registry ledger, would therefore weaken a CI gate without a user merge.

5. Fixing 4c27770 did not close this. The PR body says it took the suggestion on CI scripts outside *gate*, but the head adds only the four paths the ADR names.

The private pr-gate refs were deleted after reading.

blocking.title: D4 matcher misses CI-gate code and data: scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json, scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json
blocking.failurePath:
ADR 0021 D4 (docs/adr/0021 line 37) routes "the remaining scripts and data called by CI and .husky" to the user ("CI 与 .husky 调用的其余脚本和数据"). Its premortem names "an agent edits the gate so it passes" ("agent 改闸让自己过闸"). The script's own comment (lines 25-26) says D4 routing is decided in code so that it "does not depend on a reviewer remembering it".

The main-branch CI check job runs scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs, ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs and ui-drift-gate.mjs. All three import their comment stripping and hashing from scripts/ui-normalize.mjs (ui-registry-gate.mjs:79, ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs:54, ui-drift-gate.mjs:69). ui-registry-gate.mjs:84-87 also reads its manifest and hash ledger from scripts/ui-registry.json and scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json, and ui-dead-class-gate.mjs:765 reads ui-registry.json. None of these three files matches PROTECTED (lines 29-47): they are not *gate*, not check-*, not *baseline*.json and not listed.

Scenario:
1. A later bootstrap PR edits scripts/ui-normalize.mjs so that stripCodeComments returns '' or hashFile returns a constant. That neuters three required-check gates.
2. The caller passes changedFiles ['scripts/ui-normalize.mjs'], deletedFiles [] and linesChanged 3.
3. Line 96 gives matchedProtected = [], and the safety prompt (line 124) tells the reviewer "none".
4. humanReasons is empty, so line 297 returns mergedBy 'auto-merge'. Under spec 28 D7/§7.4 the session then enables auto-merge with no user review.

The ADR's own parenthetical list at line 37 has the same gap. It lists scripts/ui-consumer-registry.json but not the parallel ledger scripts/ui-registry.json.
blocking.evidence: I ran the head pr-gate.js with stub reviewers that return no findings, using the same AsyncFunction method as docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-harness.mjs. Each of these single-file changes returned go:true, mergedBy:auto-merge, protectedPaths []: scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json, scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json. I also ran the head PROTECTED matcher over all 35 files of main's scripts/. These three are the only files that CI scripts import or read and that come out unprotected. Fix: add them to PROTECTED and to the ADR 0021 D4 list (or protect scripts/ui-* or scripts/** with an explicit allowlist), and add a harness case.
skeptics: Confirmed at 3b0da7bb. PROTECTED in .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js (lines 29-47) has no pattern that matches scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json or scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json. They are not *gate*, not *baseline*.json, not check-*, and not listed by name. CI really does depend on all three. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `node scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs` (line 101), `ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs` (line 108) and `ui-drift-gate.mjs` (line 191), and all three are inside the required `check` job (lines 29-268). ui-registry-gate.mjs:79 imports hashFile/isHashShape from ./ui-normalize.mjs. ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs:54 and ui-drift-gate.mjs:69 import stripCodeComments from it. ui-registry-gate.mjs:84-87 reads scripts/ui-registry.json and scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json. ui-dead-class-gate.mjs:765, run by the dead-class-gate CI job at line 311, reads ui-registry.json. These files are therefore "CI 与 .husky 调用的其余脚本和数据", which ADR 0021 D4 (line 37) routes to the user. I ran the head pr-gate.js through the harness's AsyncFunction method with stub reviewers that return no findings and a safety changedFiles that matches. Each of the three single-file changes returned {go:true, mergedBy:'auto-merge', protectedPaths:[]}. As controls, scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs and scripts/ui-consumer-registry.json both returned mergedBy:'user'. Spec 28 D7 and §7.3/§7.4 say a go that is not routed to the user leads the session to enable `--squash --auto`, so the path the finding describes holds. The only fallback is the safety reviewer prompt asking the LLM to "add any other D4 path you find". That is exactly the reviewer-memory dependency the script comment at lines 25-26 says D4 must not rely on. The ADR's own parenthetical list also names ui-consumer-registry.json but not ui-registry.json or the other two. The failure is real.

I confirmed the failure at 3b0da7bb. PROTECTED in .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js (lines 29-47) has the patterns scripts/*gate*, scripts/*baseline*.json, scripts/check-*, lint-warning-cap.mjs, pack-smoke.sh and ui-consumer-registry.json. None of them matches scripts/ui-normalize.mjs, scripts/ui-registry.json or scripts/ui-upstream-snapshots.json.

CI depends on all three files. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `node scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs` (line 101), `ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs` (line 108), `ui-drift-gate.mjs` (line 191) and `ui-dead-class-gate.mjs --compile` (line 311). Those gates use the files as follows:
- ui-registry-gate.mjs:79 imports hashFile from ./ui-normalize.mjs, and lines 84-87 read the other two files.
- ui-consumer-shape-gate.mjs:54 and ui-drift-gate.mjs:69 import stripCodeComments from ./ui-normalize.mjs.
- ui-dead-class-gate.mjs:765 reads ui-registry.json.

These files are therefore scripts and data that CI calls, which is the category ADR 0021 D4 (line 37) routes to the user. The ADR's parenthetical list and the code both leave them out.

I extracted the head pr-gate.js and ran it with the same AsyncFunction stub method as docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-harness.mjs. The stub reviewers returned no findings, and the safety reviewer's changedFiles matched the input. Each of the three single-file changes returned go:true, mergedBy:'auto-merge', protectedPaths:[]. As a control, scripts/ui-registry-gate.mjs and scripts/lint-warning-cap.mjs returned mergedBy:'user'. So matchedProtected comes out empty, the safety prompt says "none", humanReasons is empty, and line 297 yields 'auto-merge'.

Under spec 28 D7 and §7.4, the session then turns on auto-merge without the user. The only mitigation is the prompt telling the safety reviewer to "add any other D4 path you find". That depends on the reviewer noticing, which the script's own comment (lines 25-26) says routing should not depend on. A change such as making stripCodeComments return '' would weaken three required-check gates and still be routed to auto-merge.

suggestions.title: linesChanged accepts NaN or a negative value, which silently turns off the over-800-lines rule
suggestions.failurePath: The check at line 87 is typeof args.linesChanged !== 'number', and typeof NaN is 'number'. Suppose the caller sums `git diff --numstat` in JS and Number('-') turns a binary-file row into NaN, or the arithmetic goes wrong in some other way. The args check passes. At line 276, `NaN > 800` is false, so no reason is added and mergedBy is 'auto-merge' even for a large patch. I reproduced linesChanged NaN and -5, and both returned mergedBy 'auto-merge'.
suggestions.evidence: Use Number.isInteger(args.linesChanged) && args.linesChanged >= 0 in the args check. Also say in ARGS_HELP and spec 28 §7.5 how to count binary rows ('-').

suggestions.title: deletedFiles and linesChanged come only from the caller; unlike changedFiles, the script never cross-checks them
suggestions.failurePath:
The script compares changedFiles with the safety reviewer's own listing (lines 258-263). It does not do the same for deletedFiles or linesChanged.

Trace: the caller builds changedFiles correctly with --no-renames, but builds deletedFiles without it, as `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=D`. A renamed test (foo.test.ts -> foo.test.ts.skip) is then an R entry and drops out of deletedFiles. The subset check at line 86 still passes, deletedTests at line 271 is [], and the routing is mergedBy 'auto-merge'.

The docstring at lines 71-73 and spec 28 §7.5 say the re-listing exists so that a list built with the wrong flags cannot hide a D4 trigger. That protection covers path names only.
suggestions.evidence: Have the safety reviewer also return deletedFiles (FILES_CMD --diff-filter=D) and the numstat total, and fail go on a mismatch the way unlistedFiles does.

suggestions.title: Configs that CI runs under are not D4-protected (vitest.config.ts, apps/web/playwright.config.ts, pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds/catalog)
suggestions.failurePath: ci.yml runs `pnpm test` (root vitest.config.ts) and `pnpm --filter @pacman/web e2e` (playwright test, so apps/web/playwright.config.ts). pnpm-workspace.yaml carries allowBuilds, which decides which postinstall scripts run, and the dependency catalog. A PR touching only one of these, for example adding testIgnore to the playwright config or flipping an allowBuilds entry, gets mergedBy 'auto-merge'. I reproduced this for pnpm-workspace.yaml and apps/web/playwright.config.ts. The ADR's literal list leaves these files out, so this is a scope gap and not a deviation from the ADR.
suggestions.evidence: Consider adding these files to ADR 0021 D4 and PROTECTED, next to package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml under the 供应链 rationale.

suggestions.title: skepticsMissing counts skeptics that answered on another head, but the log says they 'returned nothing'
suggestions.failurePath: At line 219, answered keeps only votes whose headSha equals the input head. Line 224 then adds every vote outside that set to skepticsMissing, including skeptics that did return an answer on a different SHA. Line 238 logs '<n> skeptic(s) returned nothing'. If a PR is pushed mid-run, both skeptics see the new head. The output then reports skepticsMissing 2 and an entry in shaMismatch for the same skeptics, which sends the operator after dead agents that never died. go stays false, so this affects diagnostics only.
suggestions.evidence: Count missing as votes.filter(v => !v).length, and leave the SHA mismatches to skepticShaMismatch alone.

suggestions.title: Three branch commits break <scope>(<ticket>): <subject>; the AGENTS.md squash recipe would land one of them on main without `closes #1401`
suggestions.failurePath: Commits ca088ce, 3944905 and 662cbd9 have the subject `docs: spec 28 ...` with no (1401), which breaks AGENTS.md:61. AGENTS.md:70 gives the squash recipe `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/<n>/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`. ADR 0021 D2 at the head says a human merging from the GitHub UI or the command line follows that recipe. For #1410, `.[0]` is ca088ce. Its subject has no ticket and its body has no `closes #1401`. This PR routes to a user merge under D4. If the user merges by the recipe, main gets a non-conforming subject, and #1401 stays OPEN, because AGENTS.md:63 says the body's `Closes #1401` does not reach the commit. GitHub's default squash avoids this: the PR title `docs(1401): ...` plus all commit messages includes e5414a2's closing line. The PR body's Issues section already tells the merger this. Rewording the commits would need a force push, which AGENTS.md forbids, so this is a merge-time instruction rather than a code fix. Fix at merge: use the PR title as the subject and make sure the body ends with `closes #1401`.
suggestions.evidence: pulls/1410/commits order: ca088ce, 3944905, 662cbd9, e5414a2, 0b67ca9, b67e340, 7f0b544, 4c27770, 3b0da7b. Repo squash settings: COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE / COMMIT_MESSAGES. ADR 0021 D2 at the head: '人在 GitHub 界面或命令行合并时按 AGENTS.md 的 squash 取法'. This was also run 2's rules suggestion and is unchanged, because it cannot be fixed in the branch.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 §7.5 says the pr-gate rules dimension covers docs/pr-review.md and attribution trailers; pr-gate.js checks neither
suggestions.failurePath: Spec 28 line 246 lists the five dimensions and gives the rules dimension as '仓规与缝纪律（`docs/pr-review.md`、biome 缝、尾标）'. The rules prompt in .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js:116 names CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, seams, inline import, any, helpers, closing keywords, subject format, banned words, emoji, ADRs and docs. It names neither docs/pr-review.md nor commit or PR attribution trailers. Commit 4c27770 says spec 28 §7.5 now states the args and the output shape, and those two now match. This third mismatch from run 2 remains. §8 calls spec 28 the only progress truth across compaction. A later session that reads §7.5 will assume the gate checks the pr-review.md scorecard flow and the trailers, and that pr-gate's go covers them, when no reviewer is asked to. Fix: drop those two words from §7.5, or add them to the rules prompt.
suggestions.evidence: spec 28:246 at 3b0da7b; pr-gate.js:116 at 3b0da7b; run 2's rules suggestion 'Spec 28 §7.5 pr-gate row still disagrees with the shipped pr-gate.js' (point 3).

suggestions.title: pr-gate-harness.mjs is a living test that spec 28 says to rerun after every script change, but it sits in docs/verify/1401/, which is add-only
suggestions.failurePath: Spec 28:254 says the harness at docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-harness.mjs checks the script's deterministic part, and that whoever edits pr-gate.js should run it first ('改脚本后先跑它'). docs/README.md:20 and ADR 0015 declare docs/verify/<ticket>/ add-only: '只增不改、不外迁'. Take the next pr-gate.js change, which pr-gate.js:27-28 already announces (P3 #1404 adds the merge-readiness gate source to PROTECTED, which changes D4 routing). That PR must either edit a frozen evidence file, breaking ADR 0015, or leave the harness without a case for the new rule. In the second case the 'run it first' check keeps passing while it no longer covers what the script does. Fix: move the reusable harness next to the script (for example .claude/workflows/pr-gate.harness.mjs, which falls under the same D4 protection), and keep only its output in docs/verify/1401/ as evidence.
suggestions.evidence: docs/README.md:20 at base; ADR 0015 line 23; spec 28:254 and pr-gate.js:25-28 at 3b0da7b.

suggestions.title: isTestFile is a single-expression helper with one call site
suggestions.failurePath: AGENTS.md:19 requires inlining a one-line helper that has only one call site. isTestFile (lines 66-67) is a single boolean expression, wrapped onto two lines only by formatting, and its only use is line 271 (`deletedFiles.filter(isTestFile)`). Commit 4c27770 inlined reviewRules for the same reason after run 2, then added this new instance in the same commit. Inline the predicate at line 271.
suggestions.evidence: In pr-gate.js at 3b0da7b, isTestFile is defined at line 66 and referenced only at line 271.

suggestions.title: linesChanged accepts NaN and negative numbers, so the over-800 D4 routing can silently drop; no harness case
suggestions.failurePath: Line 87 checks only `typeof args.linesChanged !== 'number'`, so NaN and negative values pass. Spec 28 §7.5 has the caller sum both numstat columns. For a binary file (e.g. a docs/verify/*.png screenshot), numstat prints `-\t-\tpath`. A caller that sums with Number() or parseInt() gets NaN. At line 276, `NaN > 800` is false, so humanReasons drops the line-count reason and mergedBy is 'auto-merge' even for a 900-line patch. My probe with stub agents: linesChanged=NaN gives {go:true, mergedBy:'auto-merge', humanReasons:[]}, and linesChanged=-5 gives the same. Fix: require Number.isInteger(linesChanged) && linesChanged >= 0, and add a harness case for NaN and for a negative value.

suggestions.title: deletedFiles is trusted from the caller with no cross-check, unlike changedFiles; the harness covers only an honest caller
suggestions.failurePath: The script cross-checks changedFiles against the safety reviewer's own list (lines 260-263). deletedTests, however, comes only from args.deletedFiles (line 271), and line 86 checks only that it is a subset of changedFiles. Input: changedFiles=['apps/server/test/foo.test.ts'], deletedFiles=[], linesChanged=10, and a safety reviewer that sees the same file. The gate returns go:true, mergedBy:'auto-merge', humanReasons:[], although ADR 0021 D4 forces a user merge for a deleted test file. This is the same class of caller-list error that run 2 found for renames. The harness case 'deleted test file routes to the user' (pr-gate-harness.mjs:81-85) only passes a correct deletedFiles. Fix: ask the safety reviewer for the `--diff-filter=D` list too and compare it, or derive the deleted set from it, and add a harness case for an omitted deletion.

suggestions.title: Fail-closed branches are untested: dropping the missing-reviewer check or the cap-reached push still passes 14/14
suggestions.failurePath:
The review stub never returns null, and no case has more than one blocking finding. I ran three mutants of the head script through the harness, and all three passed 14/14:
- m1 replaces `missing.length === 0 &&` at line 288 with `true &&`.
- m2 removes the `blocking.push(...'skipped: cap reached')` at line 200.
- m3 removes `safety !== undefined &&` at line 291.
Against m1, a null correctness review returns go:true. Against m2, three blocking findings, two of them refuted and one past the cap, return go:true with blocking:[]. These are the two fail-closed rules spec 28 §7.5 relies on, and a future edit could remove either one without any harness failure. Add cases for a null reviewer and for a third blocking finding past MAX_SKEPTICS.
suggestions.evidence: mutants m1, m2 and m3 each printed `14/14 passed`. My probe against m1 printed `correctness reviewer null: {"go":true,...,"missing":["correctness"]}`.

suggestions.title: The gate's only test sits in docs/verify, outside CI, outside D4 protection and outside isTestFile
suggestions.failurePath: Nothing in CI runs the harness; spec 28 §7.5 only says to run it by hand after editing the script. Its path, docs/verify/1401/, does not match PROTECTED (pr-gate.js:29-47) or isTestFile (pr-gate.js:66-67), and ADR 0021 D3 excludes docs/verify/** from patchDigest. So a later PR that deletes the harness or weakens its assertions, without touching pr-gate.js, is not a protected path and not a deleted test. pr-gate would route it to mergedBy 'auto-merge', and the gate would lose its only regression check without a user seeing it. Consider moving the harness under .claude/workflows/ (protected) or a test path, and running it in a CI step.
suggestions.evidence: isTestFile('docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-harness.mjs') is false, and no PROTECTED glob matches docs/verify/**

suggestions.title: Run-1 failure mode (head check through FETCH_HEAD resolving to main) has no regression case
suggestions.failurePath: Run 1's first blocking failure mode was in the prompt text: reviewers were told to compare `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD`, which resolves to main. The harness stub ignores the prompt argument (`async (_prompt, opts)` at pr-gate-harness.mjs:18), so if readRules went back to a FETCH_HEAD comparison or a bare `git fetch origin main pull/N/head`, all 14 cases would still pass. The fix at line 102 does work: this review fetched into refs/pr-gate/1410/tests/head and rev-parse printed the head SHA. Add a harness case asserting that every agent prompt fetches `+refs/pull/${pr}/head:` into a named ref and checks `git rev-parse` on that ref, not FETCH_HEAD.

suggestions.title: PR Acceptance leaves out ticket item '本票 PR 由用户合并（D7）'
suggestions.file: docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md
suggestions.failurePath: Ticket #1401 has five acceptance items. The PR body lists four, all ticked, and leaves out '本票 PR 由用户合并（D7）'. The Risk section does say the PR routes to a user merge, and the item cannot be ticked before the merge. Still, item-by-item reconciliation needs it listed unticked, because e5414a2 closes #1401 at merge and the checklist would otherwise never show it.

suggestions.title: Supply-chain and test-config files outside D4: pnpm-workspace.yaml (allowBuilds, catalog), vitest.config.ts
suggestions.file: docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md
suggestions.failurePath:
D4 protects package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml as the supply chain. It does not protect pnpm-workspace.yaml, whose allowBuilds map on main decides which dependency install scripts run (for example `protobufjs: false`, `'@google/genai': false`).

Scenario: a PR flips `protobufjs` to true, or adds a new allowBuilds entry. The stubbed gate returns mergedBy 'auto-merge' for changedFiles ['pnpm-workspace.yaml']. If the lockfile does not change, that third-party install script then runs in CI and on every dev machine with no user review.

Test config has the same gap. The root vitest.config.ts drives the CI `pnpm test` step, and a PR can exclude tests there without deleting a test file. For ['vitest.config.ts'] the stub run also returns auto-merge. This is an ADR-level scope decision, so I kept it as a suggestion. Adding pnpm-workspace.yaml (and .npmrc if one appears) to D4 and to pr-gate.js PROTECTED lines 44-46 closes the supply-chain half.

suggestions.title: deletedFiles and linesChanged come from the writer session with no cross-check
suggestions.failurePath:
changedFiles gets an independent cross-check: the safety reviewer lists the files itself, and unlistedFiles blocks go. deletedFiles (line 85) and linesChanged (line 87) do not; they are only type-checked. The caller is the session that wrote the PR, the party the gate exists to judge.

Scenario:
1. A PR deletes apps/server/test/foo.test.ts.
2. The caller builds deletedFiles without --diff-filter=D, or passes [], and stays under 800 lines and 40 files.
3. Line 271 gives deletedTests = [], so humanReasons stays empty.
4. Line 297 returns mergedBy 'auto-merge'.

A wrong numstat sum hides the 800-line limit the same way. Suggest having the safety reviewer also return the `--diff-filter=D` list and the numstat sum, and treating any disagreement like unlistedFiles: go false, and union them into the D4 inputs.

suggestions.title: Untrusted PR text reaches shell-capable reviewers; GitHub read-only and own-PR-only rules exist only in spec prose
suggestions.failurePath:
readRules makes every reviewer and skeptic read `issues/${pr}/comments` (line 104). On the public xiechimon/pacman repo, any GitHub account can post those comments.

The evidence dimension (line 129) runs up to three commands quoted in the PR's Verified section. It also runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the PR head, which runs the head's package.json lifecycle scripts and allowBuilds dependencies, with the session's credentials.

readRules (line 103) forbids only checkout, switch, reset, stash, commit and push in the shared clone. It does not forbid GitHub writes: `gh pr merge`, `gh pr review --approve`, `gh api -X POST/PATCH`. Yet spec 28 line 256 says workflow subagents are GitHub read-only.

Spec 28 line 255 restricts pr-gate to PRs this session wrote. The script still accepts any pr number, including a fork PR, and fetches refs/pull/N/head without checking the head repo or the author.

The only guard is the data disclaimer at line 105. Suggest:
- add an explicit "GitHub is read-only for you" rule to readRules
- have the script, or the safety reviewer, require head.repo == xiechimon/pacman and the session's author, otherwise skip the evidence re-runs
- skip `pnpm install` when matchedProtected contains package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml

suggestions.title: File names with shell metacharacters pass the args check and reach agents that build git commands from them
suggestions.failurePath:
The args check rejects only paths that start with `"` (line 91). With core.quotePath=false, git prints names that contain `$(`, backticks, `;`, `|`, `&` or `<` unquoted, because only control characters, `"` and `\` get C-quoted.

Scenario:
1. A PR adds `docs/$(id>/tmp/x).md`.
2. The name passes the check and is JSON-embedded in every reviewer and skeptic prompt (line 106).
3. Reviewers are told to read files with `git show ${headSha}:<path>` (line 103).
4. An agent that pastes the path into Bash unquoted runs the command substitution.

Whether it fires depends on the agent quoting the path, so this is not traced end to end. Suggest rejecting names that match /[$`;|&<>]/ in the same fail-closed way as C-quoted paths, or telling reviewers to single-quote paths.

suggestions.title: The gate's harness sits outside D4 and inside the patchDigest exclusion
suggestions.failurePath:
Spec 28 §7.5 makes docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-harness.mjs the check to run after any edit to the gate. That path matches no D4 glob, and ADR 0021 D3 excludes docs/verify/** from patchDigest.

Scenario: a later PR drops harness cases, such as the rename or deleted-test checks. It is not routed to the user, and as an evidence-only commit it would not invalidate a P3 verdict. A future gate edit, which is itself user-merged, could then be shown green against a weakened harness.

Moving the harness to scripts/pr-gate-harness.mjs puts it under the existing `scripts/*gate*` D4 glob.

suggestions.title: Verified section says typecheck and biome ci passed, but the pre-commit hook covers none of this PR's files
suggestions.failurePath: The PR body says the pre-commit chain ran 'biome ci ., typecheck' and passed on every commit. In .husky/pre-commit, step 3 runs `pnpm -r typecheck` only when a staged path matches ^(apps|packages|integration)/. None of this PR's 10 files match, so typecheck never ran. biome.json files.includes also leaves out .claude/** and docs/**, so `biome ci .` never parsed .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js or docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-harness.mjs. A reader of the body would think the gate script was linted and typechecked. In fact its only check is the stub harness, which does pass 14/14 when re-run. The claim should read 'typecheck skipped (no apps/packages/integration source); biome scope excludes .claude/ and docs/'.
